video_title: Jamahl Mosley recaps preseason win | Pelicans vs Wizards Postgame Interview 10/16/26

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's physical and aggressive tone
quotes.excerpt: I love how we're setting the tone right away. That's who we are, that's who we have to be.
quotes.quote: I loved it. Obviously, we have to find ways to do it when they're in the bonus, understanding how to be smart about it, but I love how we're setting the tone right away. That's who we are, that's who we have to be, that's what we will continue to be.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley likes the physical tone the team is setting early in the preseason. He says the goal is to be a team that is gritty and tough, noting that is who they are and who they have to be.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the importance of team depth this season
quotes.excerpt: Our depth is going to be the key for us this year.
quotes.quote: Our depth is going to be the key for us this year. That is going to be one quality that we have to make sure these guys understand. When we play the right way, we play for each other, we defend the right way, this is going to be the strength of this unit, this team. That's our identity. A defensive identity, that is our depth, is going to be the key for us.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says team depth will be the key for the Pelicans this season. He emphasized that building a defensive identity is the priority for this group.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on spacing and creating pressure at the rim
quotes.excerpt: These guys are doing a great job of creating space.
quotes.quote: These guys are doing a great job of creating space. Different lineups play different styles, but we're still trying to accomplish the same thing, which is touch the paint, find feet, set threes for guys to knock down. Guys are rolling to the rim, challenging our guards to continue to find them in the pocket. We see the lob actions happening tonight, so those bigs are doing a very good job putting pressure on the rim for us. I think that's going to be a big key throughout the year.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley is emphasizing paint touches and rim pressure this season. He says the bigs are doing a great job challenging guards to find them in the pocket and creating space for shooters.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's willingness to accept challenges
quotes.excerpt: They're willing to take on the challenges. I think it's very big and how connected they are.
quotes.quote: They're willing to take on the challenges. I think it's very big and how connected they are. They've done things together, not just on the court but off the court, that they stay connected, they're pulling for one another. We continue to talk about being able to celebrate your teammate and bringing somebody with you, that they've trusted the process of what we're doing and the system-wise for our defense and our offense, and they're really locked in to pulling for one another.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley credits the team chemistry for their early success, noting that the players are connected both on and off the court and are truly pulling for one another.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the beauty of playing with pace
quotes.excerpt: When that ball is flowing freely, it's fun to watch.
quotes.quote: We showed a couple clips at halftime of just the beauty of playing a little bit faster, the throw-ahead pass, which breaks down the defense, and then we moved it to swing it to one more. When that ball is flowing freely, it's fun to watch, and these guys understand that trust in the pass is going to have us a level of success if we continue to trust it.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley wants the team to play with more pace. He says when the ball is flowing freely and the team trusts the pass, it is fun to watch and leads to success.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Zion Williamson's work ethic and shooting
quotes.excerpt: He's putting so much work in off the court with Sham.
quotes.quote: Oh, I love that he shot it. Gosh, I love it. And they look good. He's putting so much work in off the court with Sham. Every day after practice, he's just done a heck of a job, and I think he continues to trust it. He knows it's going to have a chance to go in, and that's why we've got to continue to celebrate that for him because he's been putting that work in.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley is happy to see Zion Williamson shooting the ball. He says Zion has been putting in significant work off the court and the team needs to continue to celebrate his confidence in his shot.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on avoiding a back-and-forth transition game
quotes.excerpt: We want to play smart basketball, execution-wise, be very surgical in what we're doing.
quotes.quote: We've had a couple lulls. Washington is a team that you can get into that back-and-forth rat race, and that was one of the timeouts that I called, that we don't want to continue to drive that home. We want to play smart basketball, execution-wise, be very surgical in what we're doing, and the moments that you feel that we weren't getting back the right way, then that's when you pull the timeout. But it's our offense that can lead to those tough transition baskets, but the effort and the energy to sprint back, communicate, build a wall, and get out to shooters has been there over these past three games.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the team is working to avoid getting into a back and forth rat race. He wants the team to play surgical and smart basketball rather than trading transition baskets.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Jeremiah's command of the floor
quotes.excerpt: His command of the floor. We had a meeting this morning and we talked about his ability to command the floor.
quotes.quote: His command of the floor. We had a meeting this morning and we talked about his ability to command the floor, finding the time when he's going to be aggressive to go score, and finding the time when he's going to facilitate, and then calming things down when things go back and forth. His ability to do that, that's great growth for that young man.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley praised the growth of his young floor general, highlighting his ability to command the floor, know when to score, and know when to facilitate.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the energy of the home crowd
quotes.excerpt: I love the energy of the building. I think it's great.
quotes.quote: I love the energy. I love the energy of the building. I think it's great. You can tell that the fans want to get behind this team, and we've said it from the beginning, putting a product and a team on this floor that represents the city the right way, and that's the gritty, tough, get it out the mud defense, dog mentality, night in and night out. It's going to be physical. Yeah, they shot 31 free throws, but that's okay. We will clean up some of the other ones, but it's going to be a dog fight every time you step into this building.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley loves the energy from the home crowd. He says the team is committed to putting a product on the floor that represents the city with a gritty and tough dog mentality.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the balance between scoring and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: There is a balance for when you command the floor and have everybody in their places.
quotes.quote: That's the conversation, that's the film we watch. He did a great job studying at the summer, knowing exactly what he needs to do, watching great players, and there is a balance. There is a balance for when you command the floor and have everybody in their places, and then there's when you get downhill and you can attack and find and make the right read. So he's done a heck of a job of finding that balance. There's a lull for a little bit, he comes in, gets it off, gets a rebound, pushes the break, gets downhill, makes a layup. Next time down, calls a play, gets everybody set, and then there's a lull for a moment, then he comes down the court, takes a midrange pull-up that gets the momentum going back. So he's starting to understand that balance is what we're going to continue to need from him.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says finding the balance between scoring and playmaking is a major focus for his lead guard. He says the player is starting to understand when to attack and when to get everyone set.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on maintaining the process throughout the season
quotes.excerpt: You continue to preach it. What we're building, you want it to be sustainable.
quotes.quote: You continue to preach it. I understand it's the preseason and guys look at it maybe a little bit differently, but what we're building, you want it to be sustainable. And that's why we talked from the beginning, it's not going to be about skipping steps. The same conversations we're having now, we can have in January because it's the process. Did we crash the boards the right way? Were we right on rotation? Did we make the one more pass? Did we touch the paint? Did we communicate with our teammate the right thing? Did we execute down the stretch? Those are all process things, they're not result things, and so we have to continue to focus on the process of what we're doing and how we can continue to make it sustainable and consistent for each one of these guys. So the conversations won't stop from now until the end of the year.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the team is focused on the process rather than the results. He wants to ensure their habits are sustainable and consistent from the preseason through the end of the year.
